labels.name: Input Validation
labels.description: Failures to properly verify, filter, or sanitize data received from external sources before processing.

labels.name: Injection Flaws
labels.description: Broad category where untrusted data is sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query.

labels.name: SQL Injection
labels.description: Malicious SQL queries are injected to manipulate the database.

labels.name: Command Injection
labels.description: Unvalidated input is used to construct system shell commands. Covers OS Command Injection.

labels.name: Code Injection
labels.description: Unvalidated input is executed as code by the application's interpreter (e.g., PHP, Python, Java).

labels.name: Cross-site Scripting
labels.description: Malicious scripts are injected into web pages and executed in the victim's browser.

labels.name: Path Traversal
labels.description: Manipulation of file paths (e.g., '../') to access files or directories outside the intended scope.

labels.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
labels.description: Unsafe restoration of objects from data streams, leading to RCE or logic manipulation.

labels.name: Request Handling
labels.description: Flaws in how an application constructs and sends requests to other network components.

labels.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
labels.description: The server is coerced into making requests to unintended internal or external resources.

labels.name: Access Control
labels.description: Weaknesses in the mechanisms used to verify identity and enforce permissions across the network.

labels.name: Broken Authentication
labels.description: Vulnerabilities in login or session management allowing attackers to compromise passwords or identity tokens.

labels.name: Improper Authorization
labels.description: Failure to restrict access to sensitive resources or functions based on defined user privilege levels.

labels.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
labels.description: Unverified requests are executed on behalf of an authenticated user without their consent.

labels.name: Memory
labels.description: Low-level errors related to the insecure management of system memory, typically in compiled languages.

labels.name: Memory Corruption
labels.description: Flaws that allow attackers to modify memory contents to alter the execution flow of a program.

labels.name: Buffer Overflow
labels.description: Writing data past buffer boundaries on the stack or heap.

labels.name: Use After Free
labels.description: Accessing memory after it has been explicitly freed. A specific memory corruption distinct from overflows.

labels.name: Memory Disclosure
labels.description: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to read data from memory locations they should not access.

labels.name: Out-of-bounds Read
labels.description: Reading data past allocated memory boundaries. Use this for memory-based information leaks.

labels.name: Resource Management
labels.description: Improper handling of limited system resources such as CPU, memory, disk space, or network bandwidth.

labels.name: Resource Exhaustion
labels.description: Uncontrolled consumption of system resources like CPU or bandwidth, leading to a denial of service.

labels.name: Memory Leak
labels.description: Failure to release memory after it is no longer needed, eventually leading to system instability or crashes.

labels.name: Misconfiguration
labels.description: Security weaknesses arising from incorrect settings or incomplete deployment of security controls.

labels.name: Insecure Defaults
labels.description: Deployment of software with overly permissive permissions or factory-preset credentials that are well-known.

labels.name: Weak Cryptography
labels.description: Use of obsolete or flawed encryption algorithms that fail to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of data.

labels.name: Information Exposure
labels.description: Accidental disclosure of technical details or sensitive system data through error messages or metadata.
